Definition: from G1722 and G5401; in fear, i.e. alarmed:--affrighted, afraid, tremble.
BiblicalUsage: Emphobos is fear that takes hold of you — Cornelius was afraid when the angel stood before him in Acts 10:4, the women at the tomb were afraid and bowed their faces to the earth in Luke 24:5, and Felix trembled as Paul reasoned of righteousness and judgment to come in Acts 24:25. Even the remnant in Revelation 11:13 were affrighted by the earthquake and gave glory to God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe fear is the right first response to meeting God, but it is never meant to be the last — the angel's first word to Cornelius was an answer to prayer, and the women's fear turned to joy at the empty tomb. I hold that godly fear drives us toward God, never away from Him.
